h: How to give yourselves the best shot
p: Good escape room teams have a few habits in common. They keep found items in one spot so nothing goes missing, they say out loud what they've solved, and they don't waste ages forcing a lock that clearly isn't ready yet. If a puzzle has you stumped for a few minutes, swap someone fresh onto it. A new pair of eyes cracks more clues than ten minutes of staring ever does.

Group size matters too. Too few and you'll be stretched; too many and people end up standing about. If you've got a big party, splitting across two rooms and comparing times afterwards adds a fun bit of rivalry to the occasion.

Being on Cannon Street puts you right in the middle of the city, so there's loads to pair it with beyond the shops. St Philip's Cathedral, with its Burne-Jones stained glass, sits just around the corner in its leafy churchyard. A short walk takes you to Victoria Square with the Council House and the Town Hall, then on to Centenary Square and the striking Library of Birmingham. The Jewellery Quarter is reachable on foot or by tram if you fancy a nose round its workshops, and the canals around Gas Street Basin are lovely for a stroll come evening. The West Midlands Metro tram runs right through the centre too, so getting about is simple without the car.
